scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of Entrepreneurship for Breed Development of Rural Poultry
description:
The National Livestock Mission is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India in 2014. 

This mission aims to promote sustainable development of the livestock sector in the country. 

The specific component of this mission focused on the establishment of entrepreneurship for breed development of rural poultry was introduced to enhance the productivity of poultry farming. 

The initiative is designed to improve the livelihoods of rural farmers by promoting the development of indigenous breeds. 

The primary objective of this component is to increase the availability of quality poultry breeds. 

The mission aims to enhance the production of poultry products in a sustainable manner. 

It also seeks to create self-employment opportunities for rural youth and women. 

The initiative aims to increase the income of rural households through poultry farming. 

The targeted increase in poultry production is set at 10 to 15 percent annually. 

The mission also aims to improve the nutritional status of rural populations by increasing the availability of eggs and meat. 

The benefits of this scheme include financial assistance for setting up poultry farms. 

Farmers can receive up to INR 1 lakh as a subsidy for establishing a poultry unit. 

The subsidy is provided at a rate of 25 percent for general category beneficiaries. 

For Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, the subsidy rate is increased to 33 percent. 

Women entrepreneurs are also eligible for the higher subsidy rate of 33 percent. 

The scheme promotes the establishment of hatcheries and breeding farms. 

It encourages the production of high-quality day-old chicks. 

The initiative also supports the establishment of feed processing units. 

Farmers are provided with training on best practices in poultry management. 

The training includes aspects of biosecurity, vaccination, and disease management. 

Eligibility for the scheme includes individuals aged 18 years and above. 

Applicants must be residents of rural areas to qualify for the benefits. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required for participation in the scheme. 

However, a basic understanding of poultry farming is beneficial. 

The application process involves several steps. 

Interested applicants must submit a project proposal to the concerned state government department. 

The proposal should outline the details of the poultry farm, including the expected number of birds and infrastructure requirements. 

Required documents include proof of residence, identity proof, and a detailed project report. 

Once the proposal is submitted, it is evaluated by a committee formed by the state government. 

Upon approval, the applicant is notified and can proceed with the establishment of the poultry unit. 

The disbursement of subsidies is typically made in two installments. 

The first installment is released upon the approval of the project. 

The second installment is released after the successful establishment of the poultry unit. 

The timeline for the entire process from application to disbursement can vary. 

However, it generally takes about 3 to 6 months for the complete process. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

State governments are responsible for the execution of the scheme at the local level. 

They provide the necessary support and guidance to the beneficiaries. 

The scheme is part of a broader strategy to enhance the livestock sector in India. 

The government aims to increase the contribution of livestock to the agricultural GDP. 

Currently, the livestock sector contributes about 4.11 percent to the national GDP. 

The poultry sector alone contributes approximately 1.6 percent to the agricultural GDP. 

The National Livestock Mission also aims to promote research and development in livestock breeding. 

It encourages partnerships with research institutions and universities. 

The mission emphasizes the importance of developing disease-resistant and high-yielding poultry breeds. 

The government also aims to improve the marketing of poultry products. 

This includes establishing linkages with local markets and cooperatives. 

The scheme encourages the formation of self-help groups among poultry farmers. 

These groups can facilitate collective marketing and resource sharing. 

The government has allocated significant funds for the implementation of the National Livestock Mission. 

In the financial year 2022-2023, the allocation for the mission was INR 1,000 crores. 

The focus on rural poultry development is expected to create thousands of jobs. 

It is also anticipated to improve the income levels of rural households significantly. 

The scheme aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The initiative is expected to enhance food security in rural areas. 

By improving poultry production, the scheme aims to increase the availability of affordable protein sources. 

The government is also working on improving the infrastructure for poultry farming. 

This includes better access to veterinary services and feed supply chains. 

The National Livestock Mission is a crucial part of India's strategy to enhance agricultural productivity. 

It aims to empower rural communities through sustainable livestock practices. 

The establishment of entrepreneurship for breed development of rural poultry is a step towards achieving these goals. 

The mission is expected to have a lasting impact on the rural economy. 

It promotes self-reliance and entrepreneurship among rural populations. 

The initiative is a testament to the government's commitment to improving the livelihoods of farmers. 

Overall, the National Livestock Mission's focus on rural poultry development is a comprehensive approach. 

It addresses multiple facets of rural development including employment, nutrition, and income generation. 

The success of the scheme will depend on effective implementation and active participation from rural communities. 

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the progress of the scheme. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is also taken into account for future improvements. 

This ensures that the program remains relevant and beneficial to the target population. 

The National Livestock Mission represents a significant investment in the future of rural agriculture in India. 

It is a vital component of the country's efforts to achieve sustainable development in the livestock sector.
